scope: src/ — the shipped runtime, which is all this repository contains. Findings raised against an earlier, unrelated prototype are marked OBSOLETE where the defect cannot occur in the current design.

findings.title: One task can exhaust the host
findings.resolution: ProcessSupervisor: host-derived budgets with a control-plane reservation, per-execution memory/CPU/PID caps, worker caps injected into the environment and argv, wall clock, process-group and cgroup-scope termination.
regressionTests: A: five heavy jobs never overlap (max concurrency 1)
EN-R1: the pathological task is bounded by the wall clock
EN-R3: all 100 descendants are killed, not just the parent
EN-R5: the control plane can still execute while a task misbehaved
B1: budgets are derived from the host, not hard-coded
B2: capacity is reserved for the control plane

findings.title: Arbitrary shell execution / insufficient filesystem confinement
findings.resolution: ExecutionPolicy evaluated before every spawn: symlink-aware path containment, traversal and absolute-path refusal, destructive/fork-bomb/persistence/env-poisoning detection, environment allowlist with an always-deny secret list, and bubblewrap filesystem+network confinement for project commands.
regressionTests: EN-X2: ../ traversal is refused
EN-X4: a symlink pointing out of the worktree is refused
X6: rm -rf / is refused
X8: a fork bomb is refused
X11: writing a shell profile for persistence is refused
X12: re-introducing a stripped credential is refused
X16: secrets never reach a project command
EN-S2: a policy-denied command never spawns
EN-S3: a cwd outside the worktree is refused
findings.residualRisk: The implementer agent is intentionally allowed to edit its worktree and run project commands; confinement bounds it to that worktree, but a malicious project command that stays inside the worktree is still executed.

findings.title: No multi-instance protection for the event store
findings.resolution: ProjectLock: O_EXCL lease with owner identity, PID, hostname, heartbeat and TTL; stale detection by liveness and expiry; atomic replace on renewal. EventStore additionally refuses duplicate sequence/id, detects chain breaks and tampering, quarantines a torn final line and fsyncs each append.
regressionTests: EN-L2: a second instance is refused, with a specific reason
EN-L3: a separate OS PROCESS is also refused the lease
L5: a crashed owner's lease is reclaimed, and the takeover is stated
L6: an expired lease from another host is reclaimed
EN-V2: an edited event is detected
EN-V3: a torn final line is excluded, not parsed as truth
EN-V5: a SIGKILL during appends leaves a readable, verifiable log

findings.title: the heavyweight suite timeout killed nothing
findings.resolution: The heavyweight suite belonged to an earlier prototype. In the portable engine there is no such runner: every check goes through the supervisor, which owns the timeout and the process-group kill, so the defect is structurally absent rather than patched.
regressionTests: B: a hung job is stopped by the wall clock
B-3: the whole process tree dies, not just the shell

findings.title: Deploy could not prove what it deployed
findings.resolution: The portable engine performs no merge and no deploy at all; acceptance ends at COMPLETED and shipping is a separate, explicitly enabled operation. There is no deploy path to get wrong.
regressionTests: EN-E3: the task reaches a terminal state

findings.title: Cancellation did not work across processes
findings.discoveredBy: CLI verification during this phase — `zeus cancel` reported success while the process tree kept running
findings.resolution: Every spawn records its process group in an on-disk run registry under the project state root; cancel kills recorded groups from any process, prunes stale entries and records PROCESSES_TERMINATED evidence.
regressionTests: EN-C11: a running execution is recorded on disk where another process can find it
EN-C12: a SEPARATE process can cancel and the tree really dies
C13: the registry entry is removed after the kill

findings.title: A task could pass acceptance with no executed verification
findings.resolution: A required check that does not execute yields REQUIRED_TEST_NOT_RUN and the task ends NEEDS_RECONCILIATION. A project with no executable verification at all cannot claim acceptance unless policy.allowUnverifiedAcceptance is explicitly set.
regressionTests: EN-Q5: a policy denial of a REQUIRED test is REQUIRED_TEST_NOT_RUN
Q8: a required test that never ran blocks acceptance
Q9: a project with no executable verification cannot claim acceptance
Q10: an explicit opt-in allows acceptance without tests

findings.title: An intentional guard reported as a failure
findings.resolution: That behaviour belonged to the legacy validation-run guard, which does not exist in the portable engine.

findings.title: No task-level wall clock
findings.resolution: Task-level ceilings (wall clock, agent invocations, design attempts, review cycles, repair cycles, provider wall clock, and measured cost only when a provider reports one). Usage is recomputed from the event log, so a restart cannot reset a budget. A breach emits TASK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED with limit and observed usage and stops at AWAITING_HUMAN. Queue wait is tracked apart from execution.
regressionTests: TB2: total wall-clock exhaustion is detected
TB3: review-loop exhaustion is detected
TB4: repair-loop exhaustion is detected
TB5: provider-call exhaustion is detected
TB7: queue wait is tracked separately and does not count as execution
TB8: unmeasured cost is reported as unknown, never invented
TB10: a budget breach stops the task and asks a human, not silently continues
TB11: the breach records budget, limit and observed usage
TB12: budget usage survives a process restart (recomputed from the log)

findings.title: Synchronous work on the request path
findings.resolution: Applies to the legacy control-plane HTTP server, which is not part of the portable product. The CLI has no request path.

findings.title: EventStore.append is O(n) per write
regressionTests: ES1: appends stay flat as history grows (no full rescan)
ES2: the whole history is present and verifies
ES4: tamper detection still works with an index
ES5: a second store instance appends correctly after an external write
ES6: a torn final line is still excluded
ES7: appends resume correctly after a repair
findings.resolution: append() keeps a durable per-task cursor (last sequence, last id, log byte length) plus an in-memory id set, so a normal append no longer rescans history. The cursor is invalidated by any byte-length mismatch, so an out-of-band write falls back to a full scan rather than trusting a stale number. verify() still walks the whole chain; fsync, duplicate refusal, tamper detection and torn-line quarantine are unchanged.

findings.title: Crash recovery re-runs whole phases
findings.resolution: Deliberate policy, documented per phase in docs/RECOVERY.md. DESIGN and REVIEW are read-only (SAFE_AUTO_RETRY), VERIFY is repeatable (SAFE_AUTO_RESUME), IMPLEMENT/FIX/FINAL_ACCEPTANCE are side-effecting (REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION), merge/deploy would be NEVER_AUTO_RESUME. Nothing auto-resumes today: the residual cost is operator time after a crash, versus duplicated side effects on a user repository if it were automated.
regressionTests: EN-C7: a crash mid-phase is visible as a started-but-unfinished phase
EN-C8: the dirty worktree is preserved, not reset
EN-C9: the log still verifies after the crash
EN-C10: missing final JSON is NOT read as "nothing happened"

findings.title: Provider failures escalate as task failures
findings.resolution: Provider outages (429/529/overloaded/transport) and infrastructure outcomes are classified separately and send the task to NEEDS_RECONCILIATION, never to FAILED or BLOCKED. A missing toolchain is INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, not a failing test.
regressionTests: EN-Q6: a spawn failure is INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE
EN-S4b: a missing toolchain is INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, never a failing test
EN-S4c: the same holds under filesystem confinement, where the wrapper hides it

findings.title: Tool-evidence parser produced false accusations
findings.resolution: Zeus does not implement tool-evidence reconciliation, so the defect cannot occur here. Building that layer is future work and must carry its own tests before it is trusted.

findings.title: Prediction checks ran from the wrong directory
findings.resolution: Every check runs with an explicit, policy-validated cwd inside the worktree; there is no ambient working directory to get wrong.
regressionTests: EN-S3: a cwd outside the worktree is refused

findings.title: Reviewer independence is not yet mechanically verified
regressionTests: RI1: a clean review payload is valid and carries its provenance
RI2: every delivered section is hashed for later checking
RI4-1: planner-reasoning is refused by policy
RI4-2: planner-plan is refused by policy
RI4-3: implementer-transcript is refused by policy
RI4-4: implementer-rationale is refused by policy
RI4-5: previous-review is refused by policy
RI4-6: adjudication is refused by policy
RI4-7: acceptance-verdict is refused by policy
RI4-8: area-context is refused by policy
RI5-1: planner chain-of-thought smuggled inside an allowed section is caught
RI5-2: planner design output smuggled inside an allowed section is caught
RI5-3: implementer transcript smuggled inside an allowed section is caught
RI5-4: previous review smuggled inside an allowed section is caught
RI5-5: adjudication smuggled inside an allowed section is caught
RI5-6: area context smuggled inside an allowed section is caught
RI6: a contaminated payload is never handed to the reviewer
RI8: the developer payload contains exactly what the reviewer is denied
RI9: a reviewer claiming context it was never given is recorded
findings.resolution: The reviewer payload is assembled under an explicit policy, section by section, then hashed and recorded (REVIEW_CONTEXT). Forbidden kinds are refused, and a content scan catches forbidden material smuggled inside an allowed section. A violation invalidates the review: the prompt is never handed over and the task goes to NEEDS_RECONCILIATION with REVIEW_CONTEXT_POLICY_VIOLATION. Reviewer self-report is reconciled against what was delivered and unsupported claims are recorded.

findings.title: Task ids collided across projects
findings.resolution: Task ids carry the project identifier (project/T-0001) and are sanitised for filesystem use; the short local label remains for humans.
regressionTests: ID1: a task id carries its project
ID5: two projects' first tasks do not share an id
ID6: each engine resolves only its own task

findings.title: Prototype code mistakable for runtime
findings.resolution: The prototype is not in this repository. The package ships by allowlist rather than denylist, and scripts/package.sh inspects the staged artifact before writing it.
regressionTests: PK1: the package ships only the runtime, by allowlist
PK2: no runtime source imports anything from outside src/
PK3: the repository carries no prototype, archive or vendored tree
PB1: the repository carries no archive, prototype or legacy tree
PB10-2: the artifact contains no archive, prototype or state paths

findings.title: No LICENSE
regressionTests: BR16: the package declares AGPL-3.0-only and ships the licence
PB15: the artifact ships the AGPL licence
findings.resolution: Zeus is licensed AGPL-3.0-only. LICENSE holds the full text, package.json declares "AGPL-3.0-only", scripts/package.sh ships it in the artifact, and docs/LICENSING.md explains the network clause and what it means for users, modifiers and contributors.

findings.title: Product identity rename to Zeus
findings.resolution: Every product-facing surface identifies the product as Zeus: CLI (zeus), project directory (.zeus/), user paths (~/.local/share/zeus, ~/.config/zeus), installer, setup wizard, doctor, docs, package metadata and artifact name. The old identity survives only in src/migrate.ts and the bin/autopilot deprecation shim, both deliberate and both scanned for. Git history was not rewritten.
regressionTests: BR1: no product-facing source names the old product
BR2: the CLI executable is zeus
BR3: zeus --help works and identifies the product
BR6: zeus init creates .zeus/ and never .autopilot/
BR5b: user data and config live under zeus, XDG-respecting
BR15b: it forwards to zeus and produces the real answer
BR15c: it says once, on stderr, that the command was renamed
BR11: migration moves the directory
BR11b: configuration survives
BR11c: the hash-chained event log survives byte for byte
BR11d: logs and evidence survive
BR12: migration is idempotent — a second run finds nothing to do
BR13: both layouts existing is a reported conflict, not a merge
BR13b: nothing is moved when there is a conflict
BR13c: neither copy is modified
PB13: the artifact carries no stale product branding

findings.title: An unevidenced projected metric survived into the README
findings.observed: README.md published `ZERO_TOUCH_CLEAN_RATE 92% (46/50 completed tasks: 0 interventions, 0 attributed regressions)`. This project had zero completed tasks at the time and has zero now, so the figure described no observation. It was the headline number of the product.
findings.rootCause: An illustrative sample of the metric's output was written into documentation as though it were a reading. Nothing contradicted it: `zeroTouchCleanRate` in src/validation/telemetry.ts was always honest and reports `n/a (no completed tasks yet)` with no data, so the defect lived entirely in prose. No gate compares a documentation claim against the log, which is why a projected number could sit in the README indefinitely while every executable check stayed green.
findings.resolution: The figure is replaced by this repository's real reading (`n/a`), the metric's definition, and an explicit observed-state table covering suite size, completed tasks, live-model oracle sessions and real end-to-end missions. README now states that no figure in it is projected, extrapolated or illustrative. The class of defect — documentation claiming more than the log supports — is recorded here rather than treated as a typo.
regressionTests: ST1: zeus status survives a store that contains missions
M3-15h: a caller cannot claim more than the criteria derive

findings.title: zeus status crashed on any project that had ever created a mission
findings.observed: `zeus status` exited with an unhandled ScopeMismatchError stack trace on this repository. Reproduced directly: `zeus: ScopeMismatchError: task id expected, got a mission id "zeus-public/M-0001"` from Engine.task via cmdStatus. The primary status command was unusable, and the failure was permanent once a single mission existed.
findings.rootCause: cmdStatus passed every id from `EventStore.listTasks()` to `Engine.task()`. Missions share the store with tasks by design, and M1's scope discriminant correctly refuses a mission id where a task id is expected — loudly, which is what it is for. The discriminant was right; the caller had never been taught to filter. The defect was invisible because no test created a mission and then ran status.
findings.resolution: cmdStatus filters to task-scoped ids, reports the mission count with a pointer to `zeus mission list`, and refuses an explicitly supplied mission id with an actionable message and exit 2 instead of a stack trace.
regressionTests: ST1: zeus status survives a store that contains missions
ST2: a mission id passed to zeus status is refused, not crashed on

findings.title: The provider CLI drift lane could never fire
findings.observed: `cli-version-drift` reported SKIPPED on every run of every project: 'no provider CLI versions were recorded, so drift cannot be detected'. Confirmed by grep: src/cli.ts read `providers.versions` from config and nothing anywhere in the codebase ever wrote that key.
findings.rootCause: The lane was written against a configuration key that was designed but never implemented. A check that cannot fire is worse than an absent one, because it still appears in the report and reads as coverage. The selftest's own report made it look like a lane was being exercised.
findings.resolution: The baseline moved to durable project state (`<stateRoot>/provider-versions.json`, beside the event log) in src/mission/versions.ts. First successful contact records the baseline and is explicitly not drift; a later matching version PASSES; a changed version is DRIFT and is NOT silently adopted, so it keeps reporting until a human accepts it; a CLI that will not report a version is SKIPPED rather than PASS and nothing is recorded for it. Version strings are first-line-only, whitespace-collapsed, length-bounded and passed through the event redactor, and an address-shaped token is dropped rather than stored.
regressionTests: VB1: the lane is no longer permanently SKIPPED
VB2: first contact records the baseline and is not drift
VB3: the same version later PASSES
VB4: a changed version is DRIFT
VB5: drift does not silently adopt the new version — it keeps reporting
VB6: the baseline survives restart, because it is state and not a cache
VB8: a CLI that will not report a version is SKIPPED, never PASS
VB9: and no version is invented for it
VB11: an account-shaped token is not recorded as a version
VB14: asking the question does not answer it — compare writes nothing

findings.title: The live selftest cost cap measured provider topology, not cost
findings.observed: A healthy two-provider preflight against this project reported $0.0695 and tripped the $0.05 cap as DRIFT, which would have required a human confirmation before every unattended mission run on a correctly configured project.
findings.rootCause: SELFTEST_COST_CAP_USD was a single whole-preflight constant sized as though exactly one provider would be contacted. This project configures two, one of which is subscription-billed and reports no price at all, so the cap effectively measured how many providers were configured rather than whether the preflight was expensive.
findings.resolution: The cap scales with the work performed: `selftestCostCap(contacts)` = a per-contact ceiling derived from the single observed metered contact ($0.0695) times a stated headroom factor of 2, multiplied by providers actually contacted, with a floor of one contact. The observation and the judgement are named separately in the source so neither reads as measured. The report now carries costCapUsd, contacts and costIsLowerBound; an unpriced contact keeps the total a lower bound and is never counted as zero.
regressionTests: SC1: one contact is capped at the observed contact price plus headroom
SC2: the cap scales with the number of providers contacted
SC4: the observed two-provider preflight is INSIDE the cap
SC4b: the unpriced contact makes the total a LOWER BOUND, not a total
SC4c: an unpriced contact is never counted as free
SC5: a preflight that really is expensive still trips the cap
SC5b: the over-cap message names the unmetered contacts it could not price

findings.title: Test sources are never type-checked
findings.observed: tsconfig.json includes only `src/**/*.ts`, and the runner is `ts-node --transpile-only`, so no type error in test/ is ever reported. Type-checking test/execution.ts by hand found M3-2f asserting `!validation.ok` on a PlanValidation that has no `ok` field: the assertion was `!undefined`, always true, and the check had been passing without testing anything. The same pass found four pre-existing type errors in test/setup.ts.
findings.rootCause: The suite is executed rather than compiled, and the compile step's include list stops at src/. A vacuous assertion is indistinguishable from a passing one in the report, so the suite's own green is weaker evidence than it appears.
findings.resolution: Not fixed in this cycle. M3-2f is corrected to assert `validation.valid` and now reports the codes it saw. Extending the type-check to test/ requires resolving the four inherited test/setup.ts errors first, which is next-cycle work rather than something to fold into a release gate.

findings.title: Zeus's dependency cache was counted as the task's own work
findings.observed: First live mission, task T-0001: CODE_CHANGE recorded 43 changed files, all 43 under .zeus-cache/. The agent's real change count was zero. The validator then classified binary cache blobs as hunks of unknown surface, which pushed confidence to UNKNOWN and forced a NORMAL-tier full validation.
findings.rootCause: The dependency cache is materialised inside the task worktree, and nothing excluded it from `git status` or `git diff`. Every reader of 'what did this task change' therefore saw Zeus's own scratch as the agent's work. Worse than noise: it masked the fact that the agent had produced no change at all, and it would make any declared-writes check spurious.
findings.resolution: ZEUS_WORKTREE_EXCLUDES / ZEUS_PATHSPEC_EXCLUDES name .zeus-cache and .zeus once. A new worktree gets them written into its git exclude file, and changedFiles/diff apply the same pathspec directly, so an edited exclude file cannot put cache blobs back into the evidence.
regressionTests: ZA1: the dependency cache is recognised as Zeus scratch
ZA2: so is project state, wherever it is quoted or prefixed
ZA3: files that belong to the project are not
ZA4: the pathspec and the exclude file name the same two things

findings.title: A mission's leftover worktrees made the project's own self-check fail
findings.observed: After the first live mission, PB6 (credential-shaped content) and BR1 (product-facing source names the old product) failed. Neither had failed at the immediately preceding commit. The cause was .zeus/worktrees/, which holds full source checkouts plus an npm cache, being walked as though it were the project's source.
findings.rootCause: The probes enumerate the working tree and excluded .git, node_modules and dist but not .zeus. Because the pre-commit hook runs the suite, the practical effect was that no commit could be made while any mission worktree existed — a running mission locked the repository against its own gate.
findings.resolution: Both walkers exclude .zeus. This narrows the probes to what they claim to measure — the project's source — rather than weakening them: a disposable task worktree is Zeus scratch, not project source.
regressionTests: PB6: the working tree carries no credential-shaped content outside the detectors
BR1: no product-facing source names the old product

findings.title: The mission USD ceiling could never bind
findings.observed: The first live mission spent $1.3814 in provider-reported cost and its report read `cost nothing reported`. A single agent call carried providerUsage.totalCostUsd = 0.6353065 on the TASK log.
findings.rootCause: Providers report cost to the task that invoked them, so usage lands on task events. missionUsage() reads only the mission's own log, where no event has ever carried providerUsage. costUsd was therefore structurally always zero and checkMissionBudgets could never reach costCeilingUsd — a budget that cannot fire, the same class of defect as P1-13.
findings.resolution: providerSpendOf() reads cost out of a task's log, and missionUsage() takes an injected spendOf so it stays a pure function over events. The loop and `mission report` both supply it. An unpriced usage block is still counted as unmetered, never as zero.
regressionTests: MC1: without reaching into the task logs the mission reports nothing spent
MC2: reaching into them recovers the real provider-reported spend
MC3: a usage block with no price is unmetered, not zero
MC4: the ceiling could never bind before, and binds now
MC5: and the breach names the unpriced call it could not add in

findings.title: You could not consent to the plan you were shown
findings.observed: `mission plan` stopped for consent when the plan critic raised findings and told the operator to re-run with --yes. Re-running called the planner again and accepted whatever came back — a different plan, whose findings nobody had read.
findings.rootCause: Consent was attached to the command that GENERATES a plan rather than to a plan that exists. Following the tool's own printed instruction therefore produced approval for unseen findings, which is precisely the hazard the consent gate exists to prevent.
findings.resolution: `mission accept-plan <id> [--version N] --yes` accepts the plan recorded on the log, by version, and records every finding it was accepted despite. It refuses a plan with no critique (nothing to consent over), a contaminated critique, and one the critic rejected. `mission plan` no longer accepts --yes.
regressionTests: AP1: the accepted plan is the one that was reviewed, by version
AP2: the findings consented over are on the record, in full
AP3: consent names who gave it
AP4: and only the accepted node may spawn — the newer plan is not a mandate

findings.title: A refused plan recorded that it was refused, but not what it was
findings.observed: The first live planner call produced preconditions in kinds that do not exist and was correctly refused. The PLAN_REJECTED event carried findings, version and retryability — and not the nodes, so what the model had actually proposed could not be read back without paying for another planner call.
findings.rootCause: ORACLE_COMPILE_REJECTED already records the criteria it refused. The plan layer did not inherit that lesson.
findings.resolution: PLAN_REJECTED records the normalised nodes and their count. Separately, the planner prompt now enumerates the five precondition kinds and states plainly that there is no kind for 'the working tree is clean' — the model was being asked to guess a closed vocabulary that was never shown to it.
regressionTests: PR1: the refusal records WHAT was proposed, not only that it was refused
PR2: the invented precondition kind is legible from the log alone
PR3: the findings and the retryability are still recorded
PR4: a refused plan is not an accepted one

findings.title: A required check timed out on this project's own test suite
findings.observed: unit-test (`npm run test`) ran for 180263 ms inside the task scope and was killed as TEST_TIMEOUT. The same suite completes in roughly 130-145 s in the pre-commit gate; inside a constrained systemd scope it is slower. Both live tasks ended NEEDS_RECONCILIATION for this reason.
findings.rootCause: The per-check ceiling at NORMAL tier is shorter than the time this project's own suite needs under isolation. Note what did NOT go wrong: the outcome vocabulary handled it exactly as designed — TEST_TIMEOUT, not TEST_FAILED, escalating REQUIRED_TEST_NOT_RUN with 'the check did not fail, it did not run'. An unverified change was never allowed to look like a verified one.
findings.resolution: Not fixed. The right fix is per-project check timeouts derived from observed check duration rather than a global constant, which is a change to the validation configuration model and not something to fold into a release gate.

findings.title: The execution loop cannot represent a node whose product is a decision
findings.observed: Plan v2's first node, survey-readme, declares reads=['README.md'] and writes=[]. Its output is a choice of which sentence to fix, consumed by the next node. The loop treats a node that produced no diff as a failed integration, so a legitimate analysis node can only ever fail, be repaired once, and be abandoned.
findings.rootCause: Integration is defined entirely in terms of a commit. There is no channel by which a node hands a finding, a decision or a selection to its dependants, so the plan language can express a node the execution model cannot execute. The plan critic independently flagged the node's scope; the deeper problem is that the plan was expressible at all.
findings.resolution: Not fixed. This is a design question — either the planner is constrained to emit only diff-producing nodes, or nodes gain a typed output artifact that dependants read. Recorded as a V1 limitation rather than patched under a release gate.

findings.title: Doctor reported project health without probing the project's toolchain
findings.observed: On a real pnpm-workspace project `zeus doctor` reported healthy and the first mission failed in under a minute: the host had no pnpm, so dependency preparation could never have run. Reproduced on a fixture — doctor at 5aaceaf prints `Ready.` and exits 0 against a pnpm workspace on a host with node but no pnpm.
findings.rootCause: Doctor probed what Zeus needs in general and probed it honestly. Nothing probed what THIS project's mission path needs: which package manager its lockfile names, whether that manager executes, whether its declared commands resolve in the environment the supervisor builds, or whether preparation could run at all. Third occurrence of one shape — a provider reported authenticated while every call 401'd, isolation reported capabilities from configuration rather than probes, and now project health without project probes. The standing rule is never report health that was not probed.
findings.resolution: A project-readiness section in `src/readiness.ts`: the package manager is EXECUTED (a corepack shim that resolves but fails to run is FAIL, with the distinction stated, and the resolved path is executed rather than the bare name so the probe reports on the file it found); every declared command resolves through `resolveExecutable` against `supervisorEnv`, FAIL for the required floor and WARN otherwise in the same wording; preparation is dry-run through the engine's own `describeDependencyState`, so the predicted method is the one `materialize()` would pick. Nothing installs, fetches or writes, and that is asserted. One implementation, two callers: `zeus doctor` renders it and `zeus mission run` gates on it before the selftest spends anything. The overall verdict cannot be green while a required probe fails.
regressionTests: RD1: a pnpm workspace on a host without pnpm FAILS the package-manager probe
RD2: the overall readiness verdict is not ready while a required probe fails
RD3: an absent REQUIRED command is FAIL
RD3b: an absent OPTIONAL command is WARN, not FAIL
RD4: a shim that resolves but does not execute is FAIL, not PASS
RD4b: the report states the distinction rather than just "missing"
RD5: doctor created nothing — the tree is byte-identical in shape
RD5b: no node_modules was produced
RD5c: no dependency cache was created
RD6: doctor --json exits non-zero while a required project probe fails
RD6b: and carries the typed probes, not prose only
RD7: mission run refuses while readiness fails
RD7b: it refused BEFORE the selftest — nothing was spent
RD8b: the contract line names the preparation method and the floor

findings.title: Coverage was nominal, so a plan that could not move a criterion passed validation
findings.observed: A criterion read over a whole source tree (126 errors); the accepted plan's single node wrote one file (7 errors). CRITERION_UNCOVERED was satisfied and the mission reported an honest FAILED after $4.87, for a mismatch visible in the plan before any task ran.
findings.rootCause: Coverage asks whether SOME node names the criterion. That is not the same question as whether the plan's write surface is large enough to move it, and nothing asked the second question.
findings.resolution: validatePlan compares each required criterion's evaluator scope against the union of its covering nodes' writes, and raises a NON-BLOCKING CRITERION_SCOPE_MISMATCH. The plan critic is asked the same question in words. Non-blocking because a plan may legitimately intend partial progress; what must not happen is paying for it unknowingly.
regressionTests: SM1: a criterion read over src/ and a plan that writes one file inside it is flagged
SM1c: it is NON-BLOCKING — the plan may intend partial progress
SM1d: coverage is satisfied and the plan still validates
SM2: a plan whose glob covers the scope raises nothing
SM2c: an evaluator with no extractable path raises nothing — no guessing
SM3: the critic prompt asks, per required criterion, whether the writes can move it

findings.title: The scope extractor parsed inline program source as filesystem paths
findings.observed: The first real plan the new check ever saw produced NINE findings quoting fragments of minified JavaScript as if they were directories — 'TS(\\d+)/);return', 'm=l.match(/error', 'r=spawnSync(process.execPath,[tsc,...'. The criteria used inline `node -e '<program>'` probes.
findings.rootCause: Any token containing a slash was treated as a path. Source code is dense with slashes that are not paths: regex literals, division, path fragments inside string literals. Self-inflicted, and the exact failure the design was supposed to refuse — a false signal here teaches the reader to skip the section, which is worse than having no section.
findings.resolution: An evaluator whose text looks like a program yields NO scope at all, and a token carrying punctuation a shell path does not carry is rejected outright. Verified against the real plan that produced the nine findings: re-planned, zero scope findings, while the genuine argument-vector case still extracts.
regressionTests: SM2f2: an inline program yields no scope at all
SM2f3: a regex literal is not a directory
SM2f4: a path inside code punctuation is not extracted
SM2f5: and a genuine argument vector still yields its scope

findings.title: A mission budget sized for one repository killed plans at task five
findings.observed: maxTasks defaulted to a figure sized for small goals. A large repository's honest plan needs many more nodes — the real one needed 11, then 14, roughly one per error cluster — and would have died mid-flight having spent the money to get there.
findings.rootCause: Nothing compared the plan against the budget before acceptance, so the budget was discovered by exhausting it.
findings.resolution: negotiateBudget compares node count plus one repair against maxTasks, and the planner's summed estimate against the ceiling, before acceptance. The planner prompt now states estimatedCost is in dollars, since a number with no unit cannot be compared. Estimates are labelled ESTIMATES and never counted as spend; absent estimates raise no cost stop and zero is treated as absent rather than free. A raise is a MISSION_BUDGET_REVISED event so it survives the recomputation-from-log that makes budgets restart-safe, and --raise-budget is a separate decision from --yes.
regressionTests: BN2: seven nodes against a budget of five does not fit
BN2b: the rendering states both numbers and the three options
BN3b: and it is labelled an ESTIMATE, never observed spend
BN4: with no estimates there is no cost-based stop — numbers are never invented
BR2x: the revision is replayed from the log, not held in memory
BR6x: after the raise, the plan that forced it now fits
PS1: the stop records the RENDERING, not only the finding codes

findings.title: Oracle and planner spend reaches no log
findings.observed: After a mission made several live compiler, critic and planner calls, `mission report` read `cost nothing reported`.
findings.rootCause: P1-17 recovered mission cost by reading the logs of spawned TASKS. Oracle and planner calls are made directly by the CLI and are not tasks, so their provider-reported cost lands nowhere. The mission USD ceiling therefore still cannot see pre-execution spend, which on a large repository is where a substantial share of it happens.
findings.resolution: The compiler, critic, planner and plan-critic attach provider-reported usage to ORACLE_COMPILED, ORACLE_CRITIQUED, PLAN_RECORDED and PLAN_CRITIQUED. missionUsage already summed providerUsage on any event, so pre-execution spend now reaches the mission budget. An unpriced call is still unmetered, never zero.
regressionTests: PX1: oracle, critic, planner and plan-critic spend all reach the mission budget
PX2: and it is counted without any task having been spawned
PX3: a call that reported no price is still unmetered, not zero
